name: HVT
backbones: HVT-Ti; HVT-S (DeiT-Ti / DeiT-S settings with M pooling stages); Scale HVT-Ti-4
main_result: HVT-S-1: ImageNet-1k top-1 78.00 at 2.40 GFLOPs (DeiT-S 79.80 at 4.60)
notes: Architecture-type method. The DeiT blocks are split into M stages and a 1D max pooling (kernel 3, stride 2) after the first block of each stage halves the sequence, so the token count drops by a fixed pattern with no token scoring. The class token is removed and the prediction uses average pooling. All models are trained from scratch (300 epochs, DeiT recipe). HVT-S-1 is DeiT-S with one pooling stage trained from scratch, so the DeiT-S columns refer to this model. FLOPs only, no throughput.
evidence: "we partition the ViT blocks into several stages and apply the pooling operation (e.g., average/max pooling) in each stage to shrink the sequence length" (Sec. 1); "At the m-th stage, we apply a 1D max pooling operation with a kernel size of k and stride of s to the output of the Transformer block bm" (Sec. 3.2.1); "For experiments on ImageNet, we train our models for 300 epochs with a total batch size of 1024." (Sec. 5)

name: LookupViT
backbones: ViT-B/16; ViT-L/16 (LookupViT versions); ViViT B/16 (LookupViViT); LookupViT encoder with a text decoder for COCO captioning
main_result: LookupViT-B/16 (5x5 compressed tokens): ImageNet-1k top-1 79.1 at 16.5 GFLOPs (ViT-B/16 78.6 at 35.1, both trained from scratch)
notes: Architecture-type method. The input tokens are bilinearly resized to a fixed grid of M compressed tokens (3x3 to 10x10). Heavy self-attention and the full MLP run only on the M compressed tokens, while the N lookup tokens are updated by a cross-attention that reuses the same attention weights and a small MLP. M is a user choice, the same for every image, and can be changed at inference when trained with random M. Trained from scratch on ImageNet-1k, or pre-trained on ImageNet-21k and fine-tuned. The paper's GFLOPs for ViT-B/16 at 224 is 35.1. No throughput or latency. No code link in the paper (JAX, Big Vision).
evidence: "A fixed number of tokens M (≪ N ), which we name as the compressed tokens are sampled from the input tokens, using bilinear interpolation." (Sec. 3.1); "Compressed tokens use cross-attention to “look" at the original tokens (termed lookup tokens) and gather relevant information." (Sec. 3.1); "We evaluate LookupViT on image classification while – (a) training from scratch on ImageNet-1k [11], and (b) finetuning on ImageNet-1k from a ImageNet-21k pre-trained model." (Sec. 4)

name: FPET
backbones: ViT-B/16 (ImageNet-21K); ViT-S; ViT-L; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; BLIP-base (retrieval)
main_result: ViT-B/16 with FPET-Bi-AdaptFormer: VTAB-1K average 77.0 at 13.5 GFLOPs and 2.17 ms per image (Bi-AdaptFormer 77.0 at 17.7 GFLOPs, 2.77 ms)
notes: Token reduction for parameter-efficient tuning. One merging module at the middle layer (layer 6 of 12) merges half of the tokens (98 on ViT-B/16) by bipartite matching on a checkerboard split. The keys are refined by a small learnable adapter, the hard matching uses a straight-through estimator, and gradients are not passed to the backbone. Only the PET modules and the adapter are trained (backbone frozen). Inference time is time per image measured at batch 256 on one A6000. DeiT-S is evaluated only on VTAB-1K (70.0 at 3.6 GFLOPs), not ImageNet. BLIP-base retrieval on Flickr30K in the appendix.
evidence: "our approach merges 98 tokens at the 6th layer of a 12-layer ViT-B/16" (Sec. 4.1); "we implement a differentiable matching process and refine the keys (K) using learnable adapters to achieve a more optimized matching result" (Sec. 4.2); "we halt the further propagation of these gradients to the backbone" (Sec. 4.2); "Parameter-efficient tuning (PET) aims to transfer pre-trained foundation models to downstream tasks by learning a small number of parameters." (Abstract)

name: TF-ATM
main_result: MAE-H: 44.5% FLOPs reduction with 0.39% top-1 loss on ImageNet
notes: Only the publisher abstract was available (ACM DL refused automated access, no open-access or arXiv copy found), so schedule, other backbones, DeiT-S numbers, latency and code are unknown. Tokens whose patches are close to the median representation in the frequency domain (MF) are merged into their neighbours. The abstract says no retraining is needed.
evidence: "we develop a method that is mathematically formulated to merge tokens corresponding to patches that are close to the Median presentation in the Frequency domain (MF)" (Abstract); "Without any retraining, TF-ATM leads to significant improvements over the state-of-the-arts (SOTAs), with similar FLOPs (floating point operations)." (Abstract)

name: APT
backbones: ViT-B/16; ViT-L/14; ViT-H/14 (MAE); LLaVA-1.5-7B; LLaVA-1.5-13B (vision encoder); EVA-02-B; EVA-02-L (detection, segmentation)
main_result: ViT-L/14 at 224: ImageNet top-1 87.8 at 44.5 GFLOPs and 993 img/s after 1-epoch fine-tuning (ViT-L 87.9 at 59.7 GFLOPs, 883 img/s)
notes: Tokenization-type method. Pixel-intensity entropy is computed on the input image at several patch scales, and regions below a per-scale entropy threshold get a larger patch (32 or 64 px), so the token count varies per image and is fixed before the first block. Larger patches are embedded by resizing plus a zero-initialized MLP over the sub-patch embeddings, and variable lengths are handled by sequence packing. Main results fine-tune (full MAE recipe, or 1 epoch from a fine-tuned checkpoint). An ablation (Table 7) also reports accuracy without training. Throughput on a single GPU (ImageNet on an A100 node), batch size not stated. Criterion other = image entropy. Official ICLR title differs from the arXiv title (see g7_bib_notes.md). No DeiT-S.
evidence: "APT computes entropy at multiple scales and assigns larger patch sizes to regions with the lowest entropy, resulting in significantly fewer input tokens" (Sec. 1); "We then retain all such patches with entropy below a fixed threshold τi , which is a tunable hyperparameter for each level." (Sec. 3.1); "Since APT is content-aware, the number of tokens for each image can vary widely." (Sec. 3.3); "we observe that just one epoch is sufficient to “heal” the degradation from the new patchification scheme and match the original performance of the model" (Sec. 4.2)

name: SAD-TM
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; MAE-B; MAE-L; MAE-H; LV-ViT-S
notes: Importance = 0.5 x class attention (head average, computed at inference) + 0.5 x saliency outlier score. The outlier score is per patch position, from input-gradient saliency maps and Pearson correlation between patch saliency vectors, precomputed offline and transferable between models with the same patch grid. The lowest-score tokens are merged into the most similar candidate token by an importance-weighted average. Fixed merging rate per layer. The SAD-TM-DM variant skips merging in the first ceil(rho L) blocks (rho in [0.25, 0.35]) and gives DeiT-S 79.71 at 3.0 GFLOPs. FLOPs only (evaluation on an RTX 3090, batch 128). The paper says the code will be available soon.
evidence: "SAD-TM simply employs a fixed merging rate mr per layer for SAD-TM, i.e., a consistent proportion of tokens is merged in each block of the ViT." (Sec. 3.2); "the saliency map [24] for each input patch xi is computed via backward propagation" (Sec. 3.2); "we perform a weighted sum of the attention score with the saliency outlier score to obtain the final importance score" (Sec. 3.2); "our proposed SAD-TM and SAD-TM-DM do not require any training or fine-tuning" (Sec. 4.2)

name: HAC
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT-S; MAE-B; AugReg-S; AugReg-B; SAM-B; CLIP ViT-L (retrieval)
main_result: DeiT-S (ToMe r=16) with L-HAC: top-1 78.3 at 6560 img/s (ToMe proportional attention 78.1 at 6568 img/s; full model 79.8 at 3865 img/s)
notes: Correction of the attention logits inside ToMe. Token selection and merging stay as in ToMe (bipartite similarity matching, r tokens per layer). S-HAC adds the per-head mean distortion measured on 10% of the ImageNet training set (calibration only, no labels or gradients). L-HAC (main method) uses a two-layer MLP per head that maps token size to a correction term, trained with cross-entropy while the model weights are fixed, so training = light. Throughput on one V100, batch size not stated. No FLOPs for DeiT. The DeiT-S row is the r=16 setting from the supplementary Table 8.
evidence: "we propose Head-wise Attention Correction (HAC), a method that adjusts attention scores after token merging by accounting for head-specific characteristics" (Abstract); "control token reduction through the parameter r, which specifies the maximum number of tokens merged per layer" (Sec. 5); "fh is implemented as a lightweight, two-layer multilayer perceptron for each attention head h" (Sec. 4.2); "We fixed the model weights to purely evaluate the effect of correcting the attention scores." (Sec. 5.2)

name: √r-scaling
backbones: ViT-T; ViT-S; ViT-B; DeiT-S (ToMe-trained); ALBEF; BLIP; BLIP2; LLaVA-1.5
main_result: BLIP with PiToMe (r=0.9) on Flickr30k retrieval: Rsum 567.8 at 36.5 GFLOPs (proportional attention 561.1, Vanilla 564.7; uncompressed 580.8 at 65.5 GFLOPs)
notes: Plug-in calibration that replaces proportional attention in an existing reduction method (ToMe, PiToMe, DiffRate, ToFu, DCT): merged values are scaled by sqrt(r) and merged logits are shrunk toward ln N_j with weight sqrt(r). The method has no token scoring of its own, so criterion and schedule come from the host method (bipartite similarity matching with a retention ratio r per layer for ToMe/PiToMe). ImageNet results are only in figures. The only DeiT-S table (Table 5) uses ToMe-trained DeiT-S weights with radial correction only (77.4 at 20 merged tokens per layer, no FLOPs). Latency = total evaluation time on the retrieval sets.
evidence: "Token merging accelerates Transformer inference by clustering similar tokens to reduce sequence length (retention ratio r)" (Abstract); "minimizing the leading-order decomposed risk yields closed-form corrections governed by a single factor √r: scaling merged values and shrinking merged logits toward the cluster-size prior" (Abstract); "Our analysis characterizes √r-scaling as a training-free statistical calibration under standard Transformer operating conditions." (Sec. 5)

name: Token Merger
main_result: ?: 95% of tokens reduced, inference speed +62%, ImageNet top-1 -0.4% (backbone not given in the abstract)
notes: Only the publisher abstract was available (IEEE paywall, no open-access or arXiv copy found). Meta tokens are found first and similar tokens are merged into one by reference to them. name: LTM-Transformer
backbones: MobileViT-XS; MobileViT-S; EfficientViT-B1; ViT-S; ViT-B; Swin-T; Swin-B
main_result: ViT-S: top-1 81.55 at 3.70 GFLOPs and 18.2 ms per batch of 128 after 50 epochs of mask-module fine-tuning (ViT-S 81.20 at 4.30 GFLOPs, 22.5 ms)
notes: Every block maps its N attention-output tokens to P = ceil(rN) tokens (r = 0.7 in all blocks) by multiplying with a soft merging mask G (N x P). A learnable mask module builds G from the previous mask and the current tokens, designed from a variational upper bound of the IB loss. Each output token is a weighted average of all input tokens, so it is closer to resample than to pairwise merging. Two setups: fine-tuning with pre-trained weights frozen and only the mask modules trained (light), and training from scratch (scratch). ViT-S is the original ViT (ref. [35]), not DeiT-S. Inference time in ms per batch of 128 on one A100. Batch-size sweep is in the supplementary, which was not read. Also COCO detection (SSDLite) and instance segmentation (Mask R-CNN).
evidence: "The LTM block merges the N tokens of Z into P tokens with P < N by multiplying Z with the token merging mask G(ℓ) ∈ RN×P" (Sec. 3.1); "every target token is an informative weighted average of the original output tokens" (Sec. 1); "In all our experiments, we set the value of compression ratio r = 0.7 for all our LTM models." (Sec. 4.1); "In the fine-tuning process, the pre-trained weights are not updated and only the weights in the token merging mask modules, M(ℓ), are updated." (Sec. 4.1); "the fine-tuning setup and the training-from-scratch setup" (Sec. 4.1)

name: Prune and Merge (PM-ViT)
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; Swin-T; MAE ViT-B; AugReg ViT-S; AugReg ViT-B; Segmenter + ViT-L
main_result: DeiT-S (r=0.6): top-1 79.6 at 2.7 GFLOPs and 1887 img/s (baseline 79.8 at 4.6 GFLOPs, 1153 img/s)
notes: Token importance is a Taylor score (gradient x attention probability summed over queries), averaged over 500 training iterations and ranked globally across layers. The global thresholds fix how many tokens each layer prunes, merges (score-weighted into the next important token) or keeps, so the structure is the same for every image. A merge matrix compresses the tokens before each block, and its Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse restores the full token count after the block, with pruned tokens added back by a shortcut. Main results fine-tune 60 epochs with self-distillation (merge and reconstruct matrices learnable). Table IV gives results without fine-tuning on AugReg ViT-S/B. Throughput on one V100, batch 256. Text read from arXiv v1, whose title and author list differ from the TMM version (see g7_bib_notes.md).
evidence: "Our approach integrates token pruning and merging operations within transformer models to achieve layer-wise token compression." (Abstract); "we multiply the output of the transformer block with the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of the merge matrix" (Sec. III-B); "we calculate the Taylor importance of the elements on the attention map, summing it along the Query dimension to obtain the score of the corresponding token" (Sec. III-C); "we concatenate the scores from all layers to obtain the global scores for all tokens" (Sec. III-D); "We then fine-tune the compressed model for 60 epochs to improve its performance." (Sec. IV-B)
